A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skullptor and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Relocated and renumbered content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original normal-estimation and mesh-reconstruction experiments on NPHM and Multiface, including quantitative comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds architectural ablation results, a phone-capture example, and a mesh-resolution finding.

M1.justification: The DAViD-based cross-view normal predictor, camera-pose embeddings, losses, calibration, and adaptive mesh optimization remain unchanged. The additional fine-tuned DAViD configurations are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Triplegangers training and NPHM/Multiface evaluation remain. Section S1.2 and Figure S2 add an in-the-wild reconstruction example using 12 phone-captured images, extending coverage beyond the existing controlled capture scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates DAViD ft mono and DAViD ft multi alongside original DAViD and Skullptor. Existing Sapiens, DAViD, Meshroom, 2DGS, and SuGaR comparisons remain; the original normal-estimator ablation moves to Table S1.

E3.justification: The new architectural ablation introduces single-view fine-tuning and multi-view training without cross-attention as controls, evaluated at both normal and mesh stages. Existing benchmark splits, resolutions, metrics, masking, and camera protocols remain unchanged. The phone example specifies 12 input images.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands component validation through the four-configuration study in Section 4.4/Table 3, separating fine-tuning, multi-view training, and cross-attention effects. It also adds the phone-capture case and reports no quality gains beyond 500k vertices in Section S3.2. Earlier view-count, estimator-substitution, and initialization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The added results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive architectural results: new Table 3 reports NPHM mesh depth errors of 3.53, 2.87, and 2.44 for DAViD ft mono, DAViD ft multi, and Skullptor. Section 4.3 adds a case-specific 4.46 versus 0.201 mm comparison with Meshroom; the supplement adds phone-capture and resolution findings. Tables 1–2 and the original Table 3, now S1, retain identical values. New ablation measurements do not establish same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, camera representations, objectives, and mathematical descriptions remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or new derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims: consistent multi-view normals combined with inverse rendering deliver detailed reconstruction from sparse views at reduced computational cost. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations distinguishing architectural benefits from domain adaptation, attributes broader generalization to inherited DAViD priors, and discusses potential applicability beyond controlled capture. It also expands the existing Multiface ground-truth-bias discussion with an NPHM contrast. The controlled-lighting and synchronized-camera limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section S3.2 newly discloses mesh-resolution controls and the 500k-vertex evaluation setting, alongside approximate baseline vertex counts. v3 also supplies project/supplemental webpage links. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, and timing remain unchanged; these additions do not establish a changed mesh budget or completed code release.

R1.justification: The unique cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The reduction from 70 to 69 references consolidates duplicate 2DGS entries; shortened citations and publication-metadata updates do not introduce or remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: v3 corrects grammar and terminology, updates author/affiliation text, abbreviates references, and reorganizes the supplement into S1–S4. The retained normal-estimator discussion moves out of the main text, while the overall narrative and main section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the architectural Table 3 and phone-capture Figure S2, relocates the original Table 3 to S1, and redraws Figure 5 with revised labels, markers, and legend. References and supplementary material are reformatted; other existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new architectural controls better distinguish fine-tuning effects from cross-attention benefits, while mesh-resolution disclosure improves reproducibility and the phone example modestly extends empirical support. These gains are tempered by overbroad interpretation: Table 3 favors DAViD over Skullptor on NPHM mesh angular error, 5.68 versus 5.89, despite the accompanying highest-performance claim. Overall, the evidence becomes more informative without changing the method or principal benchmark results.
